captions.detailed: A road double crankset assembly consisting of a central bottom bracket spindle, two crank arms oriented in opposite directions, and a double chainring. The outer, larger chainring and the inner, smaller chainring are both mounted to the spider of the right crank arm. Black pedals are attached to the ends of each grey metallic crank arm. The spindle and crank arms rotate continuously as a single unit, while each pedal rotates independently on its spindle.
captions.instruction: Generate a CAD model of a road double crankset with a tapered bottom bracket spindle. It must feature a right crank arm with an integrated five-arm spider supporting both a large outer chainring and a smaller inner chainring, a left crank arm, and two black pedals. Ensure the spindle assembly rotates continuously, and both pedals can rotate independently on their respective spindles.
captions.factory: Construct the spindle using a lofted square-to-round cylinder to represent the tapered interface. Model the crank arms by lofting between two cylinders of different diameters, and extrude a five-arm spider on the drive-side arm. Create the chainrings by extruding a thin ring and patterning gear teeth along its outer circumference. Assemble the components using continuous joints: one for the spindle/crankset rotating relative to a fixed frame, and two additional continuous joints for the left and right pedals rotating relative to their respective crank arms.
